text:
incident-bot: Pager: unusual auth traffic detected against prod-auth (svc-auth). 120k req/min, 18% 5xx, spike started ~1743211080. Assigned to on-call.
pagerbot: Pager assigned to jon.sre. Bridge: https://redwood/bridge/INC-2026-3743 :rotating_light:
jon.sre: I'm in. quick check — any recent deploys?
alex_p: no deploys in last hour from ci. Seeing lots of `invalid_kid` in JWT validation logs.
maria.sec: Copy. Are tokens malformed or reused? Any customer reports?
lisa-cs: Small number of customer errors flagged by healthchecks — ~40 distinct customers getting 500s on auth exchange. No P0 yet but trending.
jon.sre: 502s correlate with auth validation failures. Traces show upstream requests with unusual kid headers and same bearer prefix repeated. Could be token replay or header injection.
ops-bot: Edge logs: ~72% of spike traffic from 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.45. Geo: unknown ASN.
alex_p: Starting a capture on edge honeypot route to collect full auth headers (scrubbed storage). Command: `edge-honeypot create --route /auth/hp-3743 --capture-headers --ttl 1h`
maria.sec: Enable immediate WAF rule to block high-rate IPs and challenge suspicious UA strings. Also enable `rate-limit: 500/m` for /oauth/token for unknown IPs.
jon.sre: I pushed a short-lived firewall rule to block 203.0.113.0/24 at edge. Watch for collateral.
lisa-cs: Noting customers in flight: billing-team reported timeouts to API. CS will open a banner draft if errors persist>10min.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3743 created. Severity: potentially sensitive (auth). Notify sec and legal.
maria.sec: Assigning to sec-oncall (maria.sec) for triage. I'll grab a sample payload from honeypot.
alex_p: honeypot captured ~250 distinct token-like strings. I'm pushing first 10 hashed payloads to secure-s3 (access restricted).
kurt-legal: On call. Please preserve raw captures and list any customer identifiers. Legal prefers hashed samples first, raw only on request.
jon.sre: Running live key-check against KMS keys used for JWT verification. No recent key rotates in last 24h. Keys appear unchanged.
maria.sec: Could be an attacker replaying leaked tokens or an opportunistic scanner with malformed headers. Actions: 1) Rotate short-lived verification key (internal) 2) Force token revocation via revocation-list for affected issuance window 3) Continue capture & forensics.
alex_p: Key rotation plan: schedule KMS key alias swap now, prepare fallback if any service can't re-verify. Will coordinate with runtime-team. Command run: `kms rotate-alias --alias jwt-verify-prod --preview`
jon.sre: Rolling key swap in 2m. Setting circuit to fallback to legacy verification for a minute to avoid mass customer OOB. Notify ops if anything breaks.
lisa-cs: CS watch: if we revoke tokens there will be an increase in login churn. Prepare comms.
kurt-legal: If customer tokens were exfiltrated we need to start notification playbook. Wait until sec confirms exfil.
maria.sec: Forensics so far: no large egress volumes to external buckets in the timeframe. Edge honeypot shows repeated small requests likely scraping header space. No obvious S3 leak.
ops-bot: Key rotation completed (preview ran). Executing alias swap now.
jon.sre: Alias swap done. Services reloaded JWKS caches. Monitoring for error spike.
alex_p: Post-rotation: 5xx rate dropped to 3%, traffic rate back to baseline. Honeypot still getting low-level probes from different IPs.
maria.sec: Good. Next steps: rotate any short-lived tokens issued in last 24h (revoke), keep honeypot active 4h, share hashed captures with legal and privacy.
lisa-cs: Drafting customer message template in case we escalate. Will hold until sec confirms exfil.
kurt-legal: Standby. If sec confirms any token material in captures linked to customer IDs we’ll trigger notifications.
jon.sre: Closing active pager window — continue monitoring. I'll run a postmortem checklist and record timeline.
incident-bot: Pager resolved by jon.sre. Incident remains open for investigation. Tags: auth, honeypot, key-rotation, potential-exfil.
maria.sec: Filing incident ticket with action items: rotate keys, revoke recent tokens, keep WAF rules for 24h, review any IAM service logs for anomalies.
alex_p: Uploaded hashed captures to secure-s3 location and updated access list: [kurt-legal, maria.sec, jon.sre].
lisa-cs: CS ready to send controlled notice if legal greenlights.
kurt-legal: Acknowledged. Keep chain of custody notes in the incident doc.
jon.sre: Thanks team — moving to followup workstream. If anyone sees new spikes ping `@oncall-sre`.
maria.sec: I'll run deeper analysis on token formats and share indicators by EOD. :mag:
